bull.b: Record bookings, a 1.5x trailing book-to-bill and $1.5 billion funded backlog provide substantial demand coverage. Combined with 86% visibility to midpoint FY2027 guidance, this supports planning and production investment while reducing reliance on near-term contract wins.

Autonomous Systems supplies most quarterly revenue and is growing at a healthy rate, while UAS sales are expanding even faster. This indicates strong adoption across core platforms and broadens AeroVironment’s presence across domestic and allied defense programs.

Low debt-to-equity and sizable equity and assets provide financial flexibility despite recent losses. A relatively manageable leverage profile gives AeroVironment more capacity to support strategic expansion and absorb operational variability without excessive balance-sheet strain.

bear.b: Negative TTM net and operating results, together with compressed gross margin, represent a material deterioration in earnings quality. The weaker profit base leaves less internally generated funding for growth and makes recovery more dependent on improved mix, volume, and cost control.

bear.t: Negative free cash flow during expansion
bear.b: Production-facility expansion is consuming cash, with negative first-quarter free cash flow and another negative year expected. Although investment may increase capacity, sustained cash usage reduces funding flexibility and increases dependence on growth arriving as planned.

The SCDE segment’s revenue decline and negative EBITDA show that discontinued programs and lower sales are creating under-absorption of fixed costs. Continued weakness in this portfolio could weigh on consolidated profitability until replacement programs achieve sufficient scale.
